One website design company, researched for each city

Plenty of US website design companies have a "locations" page with a few hundred city names on it. Click one and you get the same paragraph with the town swapped. Google's spam policies name city pages that funnel visitors to one place as doorway abuse, and readers skip them too.

The city pages listed here work differently. Each one started with research into that one place, then Maurice wrote the page from scratch. You will find the commercial roads that matter, the chamber of commerce and the free small business advising nearby, and a straight explanation of why local search works the way it does there. No page claims an office in a city where there is none.

The same method is what you buy for your own business. A city page on your site should read like it was written by somebody who looked at your town, because it was.

Web design pages by region

Grouped the way business owners think about Texas: East Texas first, because that is home, then greater Houston, the DFW Metroplex, Austin with its Hill Country neighbors, and finally the Central and West Texas cities. The two Georgia pages close the list.

Web design in Tyler, TX

Tyler and Smith County: hospitals, Broadway and Loop 323 retail, the rose season, and how a local site gets found in all of it.

Web design in Longview, TX

Longview and Gregg County: plants, warehouses and owner-run shops, and a website plan for a city that searches on its phone.

Web design in East Texas

How each city page gets researched

The checklist below is the same one used for client service areas on the Pro and Agency packages.

  1. Search demand firstKeyword data shows whether people in that city actually search for the service, and how they phrase it.
  2. The local business makeupWhat the economy runs on, from oil and medicine to tourism and military payrolls, and which kinds of small businesses grow around it.
  3. Real placesNeighborhoods and commercial corridors that a local would recognize, checked against city, chamber and news sources.
  4. Free local helpThe chamber of commerce, the Small Business Development Center, SCORE and city programs a new owner should know about.
  5. Sources on the pageEvery researched fact is linked at the bottom so anyone can check it. If a fact cannot be verified, it is left out.

If your business is somewhere else in the USA

The Texas and Georgia pages exist because those markets got researched first. They are not a fence. A web design company that delivers remotely can serve a bakery in Vermont as easily as a roofer in Tyler, and the process is identical: you ask for the demo, you look at it, and you decide.

What changes for an out-of-state business is only the homework. Before writing a word, Maurice looks up your towns the same way the pages above were researched, so your service area pages talk about your streets and not about Texas.

Two things to know before you start. First, an AI receptionist takes calls around the clock and puts you through to Maurice if you ask for him by name or want to talk about a preview. Second, the prices are the same everywhere: $497, $997 or $1,997, one time. Nobody charges more for a big-city zip code.

Wherever your business is, the demo is free. Give your business name and trade, and see a preview site before anyone talks about money.

Common questions

Can a website design company in the US build my site if you are not in my city?

Yes. Maurice Johnson writes and builds each site from his base in Big Sandy, Texas, then delivers it remotely. The free demo comes as a link, conversations happen by phone, and you sign off on pages by email. Most of what makes a local website good is knowing your business and your customers, and that comes from you, wherever you are.

My city is not on this list. Will you still work with me?

Yes. The cities listed are the ones researched for this site so far, chosen from keyword data and from earlier research. If your town is missing, the research for it happens when your project starts, the same way it happened for these pages.

What is on a city page, and why does my business need one?

A city page tells a searcher, and Google, that you serve that town, and it proves it with details that only fit that place: neighborhoods, commercial roads, local resources, the kinds of jobs common there. Your own city pages would do the same for your service area. The Pro package includes 10 of them and Agency includes a page for every town-and-service combination worth having. Read how city pages work for the full method.

How do I choose a web design company in the USA without getting burned?

Ask to see work built for your business before you pay, ask who owns the domain and files, ask for the full monthly cost in writing, and ask who you will actually talk to. Dominion's answers: the demo comes first, you own the site outright, the website itself is a one-time price, and the person who builds it is Maurice. The guide to hiring a web designer has the full checklist.

Not on the list? Ask for a demo anyway

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
